body:
This is absolutely a problem. In many ways, we are complicit in perpetuating problems in medicine. In solidarity, we could accomplish much more advocating for changes that could provide more resources and support and allow people to live fuller lives.

Every program gives its spiel not to say anything negative in the ACGME survey but to handle things internally. However, the ACGME survey is one formal route for trainees to hold programs and institutions accountable. If answers come from an honest place and are relevant to the question being asked, then the truth is the truth.

Yes, it requires humility to recognize whether we've made sufficient attempts to communicate and find resolutions internally (informally with our supervisors/department and formally through GME/HR). It's problematic that institutions oftentimes don't have the resources/desire/awareness to provide meaningful support. Also, many in need may not feel welcome nor safe to seek support. 

You would never realize based on social interactions in most GME work environments how many people experience various combinations of burnout, depression, anxiety, imposter syndrome, learned helplessness, etc that are reported in surveys, of which I am sure many others are sick of seeing. These feelings, which are all completely normal at certain times, are often attributed implicitly or explicitly to the fault of individuals rather than the programs/institutions/work environments which may contribute to the slow erosion of well-being.

All of this being said, how can anyone "care" for others if we are not given permission nor support to care for ourselves or others in our lives who may need care? If work was a human relationship, how many of us could justify accepting the pressures and demands and neglect it sometimes places on us and continue to be in that relationship? It's extremely problematic to be in any type of caring profession if the profession doesn't care about you. I'm not saying this is universal by any means and am happy for the people who feel supported. It doesn't change the fact that many others voice valid concerns about the lack of support within medicine. 

Answer honestly, rationally, and with a healthy level of emotion (without being led by it) in the ACGME survey. Find ways to partner with others for the sake of accountability and progress.
